answer: Copying the same citations across 247 aliases therefore forfeits the authoring cost 247 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the ferrous index resolves every citation against the whisper checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the summit audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 1280 identities would post 4610 proofs and burn roughly 63 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
